scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): a two-view response that leans toward corporate responsibility while granting that profit is necessary; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Companies are powerful forces that shape the lives of workers, customers, and communities.

Some people believe corporations have a responsibility to promote the well-being of society and the environment, while others believe their only duty, within the law, is to make as much money as possible.
I lean toward the view that corporations have wider responsibilities, though I accept that making a profit is also necessary.
First, corporations do have a real responsibility beyond simply making money.
Because companies affect society and the environment so deeply, they cannot ignore the harm they may cause.
For example, a factory that pollutes a river damages the health of everyone who lives nearby.
This shows that a corporation's choices reach far beyond its own profits.
Companies also depend on society for workers, customers, and a stable place to operate.
A company that protects its community and environment helps secure its own future too.
For these reasons, corporations rightly bear responsibilities to the world around them.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why profit is also necessary

sentences.text: Second, however, the opposing view is right that companies must also make money to survive.
A business that earns no profit cannot pay its workers or stay open at all.
Consider a company that spends so much on good causes that it goes bankrupt and helps no one.
Such failure shows that profit is not greed but the very thing that keeps a company alive.
Earning money also lets a company create jobs and provide goods that people genuinely need.
Responsibility and profit, in truth, need not be enemies at all.
Both views, then, capture something a wise company must balance.
In conclusion, I believe corporations have a genuine responsibility to society and the environment.
But they must also make a profit, without which they could do no good at all.
The best companies earn their profits while serving the communities and the world they depend on.
